name: TS TECH Co., Ltd.
overview: TS TECH is Japan's largest independent automotive seat manufacturer, founded in 1960, also producing door and roof interior trim and motorcycle seats. The company is the anchor seat supplier within Honda's keiretsu supply network, manufacturing across four geographic segments (Japan, the Americas, China, Asia & Oceania) with the Americas the largest by revenue. It trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market (fiscal year ends 31 March) and reports IFRS consolidated results in JPY, with material minority interests from partly-owned overseas subsidiaries.

business_model.summary: TS TECH designs and manufactures automotive seats (front/rear frames, cushions, trim covers) and interior trim as a Tier-1 supplier, winning multi-year 'commercial rights' at a vehicle platform's design stage and then supplying for the life of that model (JIT/sequenced delivery, often from plants co-located near assembly lines). Revenue is production-volume driven (essentially content-per-vehicle x units built), not subscription-like; it rises and falls with customer factory output, model-year changeovers, and FX translation, and per-unit margins on any given program compress over its life as OEMs push cost-downs. A very high share (~86-89% including indirect Honda-affiliate sales) is captured through the Honda Group.
business_model.customer_type: B2B — Tier-1 automotive OEM supplier; overwhelmingly concentrated on the Honda Group with a small but growing book of non-Honda OEM business (Suzuki, Maruti Suzuki, Changan Mazda, other North American and European automakers)
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2026 revenue by segment: Japan ~25% (¥112.1bn), the Americas ~59% (¥261.3bn), China ~13% (¥56.2bn), Asia & Oceania ~10% (¥42.5bn); the Americas is structurally the largest and most profitable-in-scale segment

competitive_position.market_position: One of the world's top-5 dedicated automotive seat suppliers by revenue, alongside Adient (largest), Lear, Toyota Boshoku and Forvia/Faurecia, which together with Magna hold the bulk of a roughly $60bn global seating market. TS TECH's own franchise is narrower and deeper than its peers': it supplied 64% of all seats fitted to Honda-badged vehicles globally in FY2026 (up from 63% in FY2025), with regional shares as high as 69% in the Americas and 67% in China, versus roughly 50-63% shares in Japan and Asia/Europe.

moat_factors.description: Seat programs are awarded at the platform design stage and run the life of the model (typically 5-7 years); TS TECH has supplied Honda for over six decades, giving it engineering co-development access and incumbency that is very hard for an outsider to dislodge mid-cycle

Seat plants are built next to or very near assembly plants to deliver just-in-time, sequenced-to-line seats; this logistics/capital footprint is a real switching cost and barrier to a new entrant winning a program late

Honda holds 21.9% of TS TECH's voting rights as an 'other affiliate,' cementing preferred-supplier status, though TS TECH states it operates with independent management discretion and arm's-length pricing

TS TECH ranks No.1 among all Japanese automakers/suppliers and No.1 among suppliers in the US on seat-related patent strength (per Patent Result rankings, April 2026), supporting design-in wins beyond Honda (Suzuki, Maruti Suzuki, Changan Mazda)

moat_factors.factor: Scale/cost position versus Adient, Lear, Forvia
moat_factors.description: TS TECH is smaller and far more customer-concentrated than the diversified global leaders, limiting cross-platform purchasing leverage and bargaining power versus a broader OEM customer base

weaknesses: Extreme reliance on a single customer group (Honda) for the large majority of revenue and nearly all of profitability
Structurally thin operating margins (2.3% in FY2026) relative to peers, leaving little cushion against volume swings or cost inflation
Minimal pricing power once a program is won — costs are negotiated down over the model's life

Large minority-interest drag: overseas subsidiaries are only partly owned, so a material share (recently the majority in some periods) of consolidated profit accrues to non-controlling shareholders, not TS TECH holders
Heavy China revenue and profit exposure to a customer (Honda) that is losing share rapidly to domestic Chinese EV makers

growth_drivers: Raising the Honda-share target from 64% (end of 15th Medium-Term Plan, FY2026) to 70%+ by the end of the 16th (FY2029) and 17th (FY2032) plans by winning a higher proportion of Honda's own model programs, including next-generation seat frame architecture and India-market models

Non-Honda ('strategic OEM') diversification: sales to customers outside the Honda Group have grown from a ¥38.6bn base (FY2024) to ¥48.7bn (FY2026 midpoint forecast) with an explicit medium-term target of a ¥100bn ('100 billion yen scale') non-Honda sales base by FY2029, driven by Suzuki Group (Maruti Suzuki, e VITARA), Changan Mazda (EZ-60), North American and European automakers

New commercial-rights wins already secured: Maruti Suzuki e VITARA (rear seat/front powered seat frame) and Changan Mazda EZ-60 (rear seats) both entered mass production in FY2026; a new development joint venture with India's Krishna Group (a local Suzuki supplier) targets further India expansion

16th Medium-Term Management Plan (FY2027-FY2029) explicitly targets 'restoring earning capacity' to a 5.0% operating margin by FY2029-end (from 2.3% in FY2026) via cost-structure reform, supply-chain localization, automation/AI-driven production efficiency, and eventual ROE above cost of capital with a goal of PBR > 1x

Structural cost programs already underway: consolidation of Saitama-area plants into the Gyoda plant, ~40% headcount reduction at TS Americas regional functions, new lower-cost plants in India (TS TECH SUN RAJASTHAN) and China (Chongqing) tied to new customer wins
Capital expenditure guided up to ¥24.5bn for FY2027 (from ¥21.2bn in FY2026), signaling continued investment despite the margin trough

Adjacent/optionality businesses: motorcycle seats (Honda, Suzuki, Kawasaki, Yamaha), an e-sports 'fatigue-estimating AI seat' pilot exploring sensor technology with possible future automotive seat applications

business.description: The Honda Group accounts for roughly 86-89% of consolidated revenue (including indirect sales via Honda business partners) and effectively all of consolidated profit; any reduction in Honda's own vehicle production, platform consolidation, insourcing, or loss of commercial rights to a competitor would be very difficult to offset given the small non-Honda revenue base (~¥49bn versus a ¥442bn total)

Honda's China sales fell roughly 24% in 2025 and as much as 48% year-on-year in April 2026 amid intensifying competition from BYD and other domestic EV/PHEV makers; Honda is shutting China ICE capacity (Guangzhou plant closing June 2026, Wuhan plant 2027, total ICE capacity falling from ~1.2m to ~720k units). TS TECH's China segment revenue fell 20.7% and operating income fell 9.1% in FY2026 as a direct read-through, despite holding a high (57-67%) share of what Honda still produces there

Operating margin has compressed from 4.0% (FY2024) to 3.6% (FY2025) to 2.3% (FY2026), well below the FY2018 record of 9.1% and management's own 2030-era ambitions; management's bridge analysis attributes roughly 2.7 points of the FY2026 gap versus the original 15th Medium-Term Plan target to inflation and other cost factors, on top of adverse production-volume swings

business.risk: Minority interest drag on attributable profit
business.description: Overseas subsidiaries are only partly owned; a material share of consolidated (pre-minority) profit is allocated to non-controlling interests, so growth in group profit does not flow through 1:1 to per-share earnings for TS TECH holders

financial.description: The large majority of revenue is generated overseas (Americas ~59%, China ~13%, Asia/Oceania ~10% of FY2026 revenue) and reported in yen; FX moves are a persistent, quantified swing factor in every quarterly bridge (e.g., a roughly -¥7.1bn revenue and -¥0.6bn OP translation headwind embedded in the FY2027 guidance walk versus a ~¥150.0/USD assumption)

FY2026 payout ratio was 149.1% of consolidated attributable profit (¥90/share dividend against ¥60.37 EPS) and FY2027 guidance of ¥92/share against forecast EPS of ¥68.47 implies a payout ratio of roughly 134%; this is funded from a very strong net-cash balance sheet rather than earnings and is not indefinitely sustainable if earnings stay depressed, though management has explicitly prioritized 'stable shareholder returns unaffected by results' through the 16th Medium-Term Plan

FY2026 operating cash flow was reduced in part by higher corporate tax payments tied to a Japan-US Advance Pricing Agreement (APA) settlement, evidencing ongoing transfer-pricing scrutiny across the group's US operations

regulatory.description: The Americas is TS TECH's largest segment (~59% of FY2026 revenue) and highly exposed to any US tariff escalation on vehicles/parts and to Honda's own responses (nearshoring, platform shifts) that could disrupt existing seat-program sourcing; Americas operating income already fell 76% in FY2026 on lower customer production and higher expenses

Management explicitly cited US policy shifts forcing automakers (including Honda) to revise EV strategy as a source of 2026 business-environment uncertainty; seat/interior content and sourcing can change materially between ICE, hybrid and BEV platforms

macro.description: Revenue is a direct function of customer (mainly Honda) vehicle production volumes, which are sensitive to consumer demand cycles, semiconductor/parts availability, and OEM inventory management

Management cited rising manufacturing costs from inflation as a headwind across FY2026, compounding the volume-driven margin decline; wage inflation is also flagged as a factor in the FY2027 cost bridge

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global automotive seating market (~$60bn in 2025) is forecast to grow at a modest ~3% CAGR through 2035, a mature, low-growth industry where competitive position and OEM program wins matter far more than end-market growth; Japanese-brand OEMs including Honda are simultaneously losing share in China to domestic EV/PHEV makers, a structural headwind specific to TS TECH's largest customer
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — revenue tracks customer (overwhelmingly Honda) vehicle production volumes directly; segment results show double-digit swings in operating income from volume and mix changes alone
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity given a large net-cash balance sheet and negligible interest-bearing debt; indirect sensitivity via global auto demand and OEM capex/production decisions
key_input_costs: Steel and other raw materials for seat frames
Labor (wage inflation cited as an FY2027 cost headwind)
USD/JPY and CNY/JPY exchange rates on translation of overseas earnings

recent_developments.event: FY2026 (year to 31 March 2026) results announced: revenue ¥442.3bn (-4.0% YoY), operating income ¥10.3bn (-37.2% YoY, margin 2.3% vs 3.6% prior year), profit attributable to owners ¥7.1bn (-17.3% YoY); management attributed the decline primarily to reduced production for major customers (Honda) and higher expenses, particularly in the Americas, despite continued cost-cutting

FY2027 guidance issued: revenue ¥440.0bn (-0.5%), operating income ¥13.0bn (+25.9%, margin 3.0%), profit attributable to owners ¥8.0bn (+12.1%); dividend guided up to ¥92/share (from ¥90 paid for FY2026); capex guided to ¥24.5bn (from ¥21.2bn)

16th Medium-Term Management Plan (April 2026-March 2029) unveiled under the theme 'Restoring earning capacity,' targeting a 5.0% operating margin, 5.0% ROE and 3.5%+ DOE by the plan's end (FY2029), and a longer-term 17th-plan ambition of an 'industry-leading' 5%+ seat-industry operating margin and PBR above 1x

Presidential transition confirmed in filings: Eiji Toba (鳥羽英二) is named Representative Director, President, presenting the 16th Medium-Term Plan and FY2027 outlook, while Masanari Yasuda (previously President, named in the H1 FY2026 filing) presented the FY2026 results review as Representative Director — consistent with a CEO handover around the FY2026/FY2027 boundary
FY2026 buyback of ¥5.0bn completed (following a larger ¥15.0bn buyback in FY2025); cumulative 15th Medium-Term Plan buybacks totaled ¥20.0bn as guided

TS TECH received 'First Prize for Quality Improvements and New Supplier Award' from Changan Mazda for EZ-60 rear seat production, and in November 2025 a 'Best Partner Award and Technology Development Award' from Suzuki Motor — both signaling traction in non-Honda commercial-rights expansion

Q1 FY2027 (April-June 2026) results announced: revenue ¥112.8bn (+9.9% YoY), operating income ¥1.73bn (+14.1% YoY), profit attributable to owners ¥1.60bn (vs ¥0.59bn prior year, +172%); Japan and Americas segments grew strongly (Americas revenue +16.4% YoY aided by FX and higher customer production), while China revenue fell 37.4% YoY and swung to an operating loss on continued Honda production cuts; USD/JPY averaged ¥159.6 in the quarter versus ¥144.6 a year earlier, a significant translation tailwind

Honda continuing to scale back China ICE production capacity (Guangzhou GAC Honda plant closure due June 2026, Wuhan Dongfeng Honda plant due 2027) amid BYD/domestic EV competition — the primary external driver of TS TECH's China segment deterioration

guidance.management_commentary: Incoming President Eiji Toba framed the 16th Medium-Term Plan (FY2027-FY2029) around 'restoring earning capacity' (稼ぐ力を取り戻す) after operating margin fell from a FY2018 peak of 9.1% to 2.3% in FY2026, citing production-volume declines at major customers plus inflation and other cost factors (a cited -2.7 point structural drag) as the causes. Management explicitly separated the FY2027 guidance walk into an exchange-rate tailwind, an order-volume/production-mix effect, and an 'earnings recovery' bucket from cost actions, expecting the latter to offset continued expense inflation including wage hikes. On capital allocation, management reiterated 'giving top priority to maximizing operating cash flow' and 'ensuring sustained and stable shareholder returns unaffected by results,' explicitly flagging a willingness to use debt funding for growth investment/M&A while maintaining DOE-based stable dividends, with an ambition to bring ROE above cost of capital and swiftly achieve a price-to-book ratio above 1x.

bull_case: Balance sheet offers a large margin of safety: ¥92.6bn cash against essentially no interest-bearing debt and ¥309.9bn attributable equity, against a market capitalization of roughly ¥216-230bn — cash alone covers a large fraction of the market cap, and management is committed to returning capital (¥90-92/share dividend, ongoing buybacks) even through the earnings trough

FY2026 looks like a cyclical/structural trough rather than a permanent step-down: management's own FY2027 guidance calls for operating income to recover ~26% on cost actions and FX, and Q1 FY2027 results already show operating income up 14% YoY and net income up 172% YoY, aided by a weaker yen and stronger Japan/Americas volumes

Genuine, multi-decade keiretsu moat in the core Honda seat business — commercial rights won at platform design stage are extremely sticky mid-cycle, and TS TECH continues to gain share of Honda's own production (64% in FY2026, targeting 70%+ by FY2029) even as Honda's total volumes fluctuate

Credible, if still small, diversification away from Honda: newly won programs with Maruti Suzuki (e VITARA), Changan Mazda (EZ-60), and supplier awards from Suzuki Motor and Changan Mazda evidence real design-win traction, with an explicit ¥100bn-plus non-Honda sales target providing a second growth leg

Management has articulated a specific, numeric margin-recovery roadmap (2.3% to 5.0% operating margin by FY2029, 'industry-leading' 5%+ by FY2032) alongside ROE and PBR targets, giving investors concrete milestones to hold the company accountable to
bear_case: Extreme, near-irreducible dependence on a single customer group: ~86-89% of revenue comes from the Honda Group, and Honda itself holds ~22% of TS TECH's voting rights — there is essentially no way to diversify quickly enough to offset a serious Honda production shortfall, and the ¥100bn non-Honda sales target (even if achieved) would still leave Honda dominant through FY2029-32

The company's largest customer is losing a share war in its most important growth market: Honda's China sales fell ~24% in 2025 and as much as 48% YoY in April 2026 against BYD and other domestic EV/PHEV makers, with Honda now permanently shutting ICE capacity there through 2027 — this is a structural, not cyclical, headwind to TS TECH's China segment (already -20.7% revenue, -9.1% operating income in FY2026, and a Q1 FY2027 operating loss)

Operating margin has more than halved in two years (4.0% to 2.3%) with the prior 15th Medium-Term Plan badly missing its own FY2026 targets (revenue ¥480bn vs. ¥442bn actual; operating margin 9.2% vs. 2.3% actual; ROE 8.5% vs. 2.3% actual) — management's new 5.0%-by-FY2029 target requires it to succeed where the prior plan failed, against a similarly uncertain China/tariff/EV backdrop

The Americas segment — the single largest and, historically, most profitable segment — is exposed to US tariff policy on vehicles/parts and to any Honda nearshoring or platform decisions, and already saw operating income fall 76% in FY2026 on higher expenses and lower customer production

A dividend payout ratio above 100% of earnings (149% in FY2026, ~134% guided for FY2027) is being sustained by drawing down a strong cash pile rather than by earnings; if the margin-recovery plan slips again, either the payout ratio rises further or the dividend eventually has to be cut, removing one of the stock's key support pillars
Material non-controlling interests mean a meaningful share of any consolidated profit recovery does not flow through to TS TECH's own shareholders
